channel.title: Human Resource Executive - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Human Resource Executive (hrexecutive.com)

item.title: Pay transparency laws surge: how to turn compliance into strategy
item.description: Pay transparency laws are quickly changing, both in the U.S. and globally, prompting employers to rethink compliance.

item.title: As Eightfold, Workday suits show, AI legal risks are building for HR
item.description: Several suits against HR tech firms highlight the AI legal risks facing employers deploying the tech in their people practices.

item.title: A first look at the White House AI Policy Framework
item.description: The White House on Friday released its AI Policy Framework—a vision for how Congress should guide AI development and implementation.

item.title: 5 practical steps to creating HR shared services for your company
item.description: Even modest shifts in how HR work is organized through shared services can create efficiency gains and a better employee experience.

item.title: Mental health: 1 in 3 employees are 'merely surviving'
item.description: Lyra Health's sixth annual report finds that employees worldwide are struggling with compounding mental health pressures.

item.title: How executive pay parity is redefining women in leadership
item.description: This International Women's Day, new research suggests a narrowing gap in executive pay between men and women.

item.title: Why internal mobility is now a business imperative for HR
item.description: HR leader Aly Sparks on how internal mobility helps close skills gaps, support blended workforces and keep talent moves human in an AI era.

item.title: DOL formally scraps Biden-era fiduciary rule
item.description: Learn about the recent changes to the fiduciary rule and how this affects the determination of investment advice fiduciaries.

item.title: Why talent analytics lose accuracy after day one: The post-hire blind spot
item.description: Hiring the right person, and the right outcomes follow. The science behind selection is sound. What happens next is not measured at all.

item.title: New state regs are a 'blueprint' for discriminatory AI claims
item.description: Illinois, New York and Colorado are driving a wave of AI employment law. HR leaders need a keen eye on bias, audits and vendor liability.
